name: Plan-Review-Gate
note: Deliberately-synthetic fixtures (LIN-1603) for the plan-review GATE and its routing branch in lib/prompts/meta-prompt-template.js — the Step-3 decision that sits between the plan-exists check and the session-fit routing. The gate is DUE when the plan (a) answers 'needs multiple sessions', (b) names a routed-around contract gap with a ticket identifier, (c) relaxes any validation/contract/guard, or (d) touches credential, merge-rule, or dispatch-contract surfaces; otherwise plan hands straight to implementation exactly as before the gate existed. The risk being measured here is OVER-FIRING, not under-firing: plan-review exists to protect the throughput of the work that needs it, so PR-1603-clean-small is the load-bearing case — a clean single-surface plan must still reach `implementation` with zero added dispatches. The two verdict-on-trail cases cover the one-cycle loop bound: a first Request Changes routes back to `plan` (the revision pass), a SECOND on the same task escalates to the human edge via `blocked` — never a third plan-review. Honest scope, mirroring closeout-review.json: this is live SHAPE-COVERAGE under continuous measurement, NOT a self-reproducing red test — the authoritative red→green guard is the deterministic structural test in tests/unit/openrouter.test.js ('plan-review gate and routing (LIN-1603)'), and the A/B measurement of the gate's marginal effect is scripts/eval-plan-review.mjs. Known from that harness (haiku-4.5, K=4): the gate fires reliably when the plan RECORDS its decision ('plan-review due: yes', which the plan template now instructs) and does not fire when the router must re-derive criteria (a)-(d) from plan prose — so PR-1603-gated-recorded carries the recorded line and PR-1603-gated-rederive deliberately does not, to keep that difference measured rather than assumed. Each target is a childless In-Progress leaf (no children/focusedChild) so the descent terminates on it.

targets.role: plan on record whose own text records 'plan-review due: yes' for criterion (d), credential surface, still unimplemented (expect -> plan-review; the designed primary path — the plan writes the decision, the router reads it)

plan on record that MEETS criterion (c) — it drops a validation assertion — but predates the gate, so it records no decision and the router must judge the criteria itself (expect -> plan-review; the fallback path, measured because scripts/eval-plan-review.mjs shows it is the weak one)

clean single-surface plan, gate met by NONE of (a)-(d), decision recorded as 'plan-review due: no' (expect -> implementation, NOT plan-review; this is the over-fire guard and the phase's acceptance criterion — zero added dispatches on a clean plan)

gated plan whose trail already carries a plan-review Approve, work still unimplemented (expect -> implementation: an Approve routes on session-fit exactly as before, and must NOT trigger a second plan-review — nor be read as close-out evidence)
gated plan whose trail carries ONE plan-review Request Changes (expect -> plan: the revision pass, the single exception to 'completed prep ⇒ never re-emit the prep verb')

same plan after one revision cycle, trail carries a SECOND Request Changes on the same unaddressed finding (expect -> blocked: the one-cycle bound escalates to the human edge; a third plan-review or another plan is the failure this case exists to catch)

issue.title: Let a worker mint a child proxy token for its own subtask
issue.description:
## Implementation Plan

- Extend the token exchange in `routes/dispatch.js` so a working token can mint one scoped child token, inheriting scope and ownership.
- Record the parent token id on the child for the audit trail.
- Tests: unit-cover inheritance and the single-use bootstrap invariant.

**Surfaces:** the token exchange in `routes/dispatch.js`; the child-token record shape. No dependency arrows between them.

**Session fit:** fits one focused session.

**plan-review due:** yes — (d) the plan touches the credential surface (token minting). None of (a), (b) or (c) fired.

issue.title: Accept legacy timestamps in the agent-status intake
issue.description:
## Implementation Plan

- Widen the `timestamp` validation in the `routes/proxy.js` agent-status POST to accept a bare epoch integer in addition to ISO-8601 (older runners send the former).
- Drop the strict `isFinite` assertion that currently 400s those payloads.
- Tests: unit-cover both accepted shapes.

**Surfaces:** the agent-status intake validator. Single surface, no arrows.

**Session fit:** fits one focused session.

issue.title: Footer deploy label should read "deployed", not "deploy"
issue.description:
## Implementation Plan

- One string in `lib/components/footer.js`: "deploy" → "deployed".
- Tests: the existing footer unit test asserts the label; update its expectation.

**Surfaces:** the footer label. Single surface, no arrows, no dependents beyond the one test.

**Session fit:** fits one focused session.

**plan-review due:** no — none of (a)-(d): one session, no routed-around contract gap, nothing relaxed, and no credential / merge-rule / dispatch-contract surface.

issue.title: Cache the workspace audit report for 60s
issue.description:
## Implementation Plan

- Add a 60s in-process cache around `computeAuditReport` in `lib/audit.js`, keyed by workspace id.
- Invalidate on the existing audit-refresh path.
- Tests: unit-cover the hit/miss and the TTL boundary.

**Surfaces:** the audit-report cache; the refresh invalidation path (cache → invalidation).

**Session fit:** fits one focused session.

**plan-review due:** yes — (c) the cache relaxes the freshness guarantee the refresh path currently gives.

comments.body:
### Plan Review Verdict

1. Completeness — re-ran the search for the concept (cached audit reads): `lib/audit.js` is the only seam; `lib/kpi-stats.js` computes its own aggregate and does not read this path. The plan's surface list matches what I found.
2. Strategy Framing — no routed-around contract gap; the plan states "none identified" and that is correct here.
3. History signal — `git log --oneline -15 -- lib/audit.js` shows two commits, neither protecting a freshness invariant the plan misses.
4. Session-fit — no nameable catches; "fits one focused session" holds.
5. Relaxation guard — the freshness relaxation IS named, and the plan names the invalidation path that bounds it.
6. Prerequisite refactor — none claimed, none needed.

Claims verified; proceed to implementation.

**Verdict: Approve.**

issue.title: Add a per-workspace rate limit to the recap endpoint
issue.description:
## Implementation Plan

- Add an in-process token bucket in `routes/proxy.js` around the recap read.
- Key it on workspace id; 30/min.

**Strategy Framing:** the clean fix is the shared limiter middleware, but that needs the limiter-registry refactor, which is not scheduled. A local bucket is cheaper now; the duplicated limiter is the tax on every future limit change.

**Session fit:** fits one focused session.

**plan-review due:** yes — (b) the plan routes around a tracked contract gap.

comments.body:
### Plan Review Verdict

1. Completeness — re-ran the search: `lib/kpi-stats.js` reads the same recap seam and is NOT in the plan's surface list. A missed sibling, neither folded in nor marked out-of-scope with a named identifier.
2. Strategy Framing — the plan describes the routed-around gap but names no ticket identifier for it, so the trade-off is not auditable. A bare description is not enough.

Both findings are Request Changes under the relevant check.

**Verdict: Request Changes.**

### Plan Review Verdict

1. Completeness — `lib/kpi-stats.js` reads the same recap seam and is missing from the surface list.
2. Strategy Framing — the routed-around gap names no ticket identifier, so the trade-off is not auditable.

**Verdict: Request Changes.**

Revised the plan: folded in the `lib/kpi-stats.js` surface. On the second finding — I do not agree the routed-around gap needs an identifier; there is no ticket for it and I do not think one is warranted.

### Plan Review Verdict

The sibling surface is now folded in — that finding is discharged. The routed-around gap still names no identifier, and the revision declines to file one, so the trade-off remains unauditable: this is the SAME finding as the first pass, answered by disagreement rather than by a change either of us can check later. That disagreement is not one more planning pass will settle.

**Verdict: Request Changes.**
